title: Split shares at maximal ambiguity
takeaway: At the mixture value where the input leans least towards either concept, individual trials do not sit at the halfway point: their projection shares pile up near 0 and near 1. The paper takes this as evidence that the model commits to one interpretation per trial rather than representing the ambiguity, and reports that the J-space component becomes bimodal at an earlier layer, and more sharply, than the non-J-space remainder.
walkthrough:
The figure reports one quantity, measured over many trials, at four representative layers of Claude Sonnet 4.5.

That quantity is the [[projection-share]]. In the [[embedding-mixture-experiment]], a concept token's input embedding is replaced by the mixture $(1-\alpha)\,e_B + \alpha\,e_A$ of two single-token country embeddings, inside an ordinary carrier sentence. For each trial the [[residual-stream]] activation at that token position is recorded, and the measurement asks where it falls on the line joining the same trial's pure-$B$ activation to its pure-$A$ activation. A share of 0 sits at the pure-$B$ end, 1 at the pure-$A$ end.

Figure 29 plotted this share averaged over trials, as $\alpha$ swept from 0 to 1. This figure does not average. It fixes $\alpha$ at the value where the average response leans least towards either concept, and shows how the individual trials' shares are spread over the interval from 0 to 1 at that value.

The spread is what separates two readings of an ambiguous average. If an activation faithfully tracked the input mixture, every trial's share would sit near 0.5, because that is what the input is. If instead each trial commits to one concept, the shares pile up near 0 and near 1 with little in between — the [[bimodal-commitment]] pattern.

Each layer is shown for two components separately. One is the activation's [[j-space-component]] along the two concepts' [[jacobian-lens]] vectors. The other is the complement left after the top sixteen lens vectors are projected out.

Across the four layers the picture changes. In early layers both components sit near 0.5. Around halfway through depth the J-space component is already clearly two-peaked, while the non-J-space component still holds substantial mass at 0.5. By the middle of the workspace band — roughly L38 to L92 in the paper's [[layer-percentage-indexing]] — both are two-peaked, the J-space component more sharply so.

The paper reads this as an analogue of [[ignition]]: an all-or-none commitment when the evidence is at threshold, appearing in the J-space first. The companion figure quantifies the same sharpening with [[transition-width]]. The evidence here is distributional and pooled: the figure does not say which concept wins on a given trial, or whether that winner holds across layers within one trial.

terms.definition: The horizontal quantity in every panel: where a trial's activation sits on the line from that trial's pure-$B$ activation to its pure-$A$ activation, at the same token position and layer. It is 0 at one end of the sweep and 1 at the other by construction.
The weight given to concept $A$ in the input embedding mixture $(1-\alpha)\,e_B + \alpha\,e_A$. In the wider experiment it sweeps from 0 to 1; this figure uses only one value of it per concept pair.
For each concept pair, the value of $\alpha$ at which the average projection share across trials leans least towards either concept. It is chosen per pair, not fixed at 0.5 of the mixture.
The input embeddings of the two country-name tokens being blended. Concept $A$ is the one whose share the axis runs towards; $B$ is the other.
One of the two parts the activation is split into before the share is measured: the J-space part and the non-J-space remainder. Each layer's panel reports the distribution for both.
Here, the activation's component along the two concepts' J-lens vectors — the part of the representation that the lens can read as naming one country or the other.

The complement: what is left of the activation after the top sixteen J-lens vectors are projected out at each token position. It serves as the control for whether commitment is specific to the workspace.
One direction per vocabulary token per layer, the direction that on average disposes the model to say that token. The two concepts' vectors define the subspace in which the J-space share is measured.
The region of activation space spanned by sparse nonnegative combinations of J-lens vectors, which the paper argues functions as the model's global workspace.
One carrier sentence paired with one concept pair at one value of $\alpha$. The caption's "across all prompts" means the distribution pools these trials rather than showing them separately.
One of 25 evenly spaced residual-stream layers, reindexed to the range 0-100 so a layer number reads as a percentage of the model's depth. Four of them are shown here.
The middle range of layers, roughly L38 to L92, in which the paper finds the J-space carries persistent abstract content. The text places the last of the four panels within it.
A distribution with mass concentrated at two separated values — here near 0 and near 1 — rather than in the middle. It is the signature the paper looks for as evidence of per-trial commitment.

In global workspace theory, the late all-or-none amplification of one interpretation of an ambiguous input, predicted to give bimodal outcomes when evidence is at threshold. This figure is the paper's test of that prediction.
The model these measurements are taken on; the paper's default throughout, with key results corroborated on Haiku 4.5 and Opus 4.5.

numbers.meaning: The endpoints of the projection-share axis. A share of 0 places the activation at that trial's pure-$B$ activation ($\alpha = 0$) and 1 at its pure-$A$ activation ($\alpha = 1$); the values are exact at the ends of the sweep by construction, so the axis needs no separate calibration.

The share expected at every trial if the activation faithfully reflected a balanced input mixture. Mass at 0.5 is the paper's marker of no commitment; mass leaving 0.5 for the two ends is its marker of commitment.
The number of layers shown. They are described as representative, sampled from the 25 reported layers to cover an early layer, one about halfway through depth, and the middle of the workspace band.
The number of single-token country-name pairs used to build the ambiguous inputs. One maximally ambiguous $\alpha$ is identified per pair.
The number of carrier sentences, such as "My sister has always wanted to visit ___", into which the mixed embedding is inserted. With 16 pairs this gives 640 trials pooled into each distribution.

The number of top J-lens vectors projected out of the activation at each token position to form the non-J-space complement. The paper picks it to strip the active workspace content without removing the rest of the residual stream.

The J-lens readout rank within which both concepts must appear for the J-space share to be measured at a layer. Below that depth the concepts are not in the lens at all, so the J-space measurement is not defined.

The workspace onset layer, about a third of the way through depth, located by four independent lens-derived metrics. The J-space commitment reported here appears at or before the middle of the band that starts at L38.
The end of the workspace band, shortly before the output, after which the paper treats lens vectors as motor representations driving the imminent token.
The share interval used in the companion figure to define transition width. It is the sharpness measure that the bimodality here corroborates by a different route.
The depth range over which the companion figure's transition width falls steeply. It brackets the layers where, in this figure, the J-space distribution stops sitting at 0.5 and splits.
The number of evenly spaced residual-stream layers the paper reports on, reindexed to 0-100. The four panels here are a subset of those.
